messages.subject: Mediation Using CATEGORICAL EXOGENOUS, CATEGORICAL ENDOGENOUS
parts:
Hi,

My data set consists on 30+ question (1-7 likert scale) and I have transformed them into LATENT VARIABLES 6 which regress on Y (GLOBAL SATISFACTION)
I have run SEM analysis using lavaan and I am getting good results.

The data is on perception of global satisfaction with a transit system

Also ran the measurement invariance test, and it is coming significant for the weak invariance, for the 4 different surveys done. This means that the model is measurement models is OK.
Now my hypothesis is that different groups of people perceive certain latent variables with more importance than others.
I have the following CATEGORIES (EXOGE)
GSE socioeconomic factor
AGE
SEX
TIME (morning peak, afternoon peak, valley)
DAY (week, sat, sunday)
FREQUENT transit user
FREQUENT metro user

First I want to check if there is interaction between the 6LVs--> CAT(EXO) --> Y
I am fairly new to SEM but understand I need to somehow transform the CATS into numbers?

Second, I have two ENDOG CATS Perceived Waiting Time and Perceived Travel Time.
I also think there will be major changes in the models for theses CATS, here I just want to check if there are significant differences between the models obtained.
I think no mediation but I am uncertain.

Thanks for any help given.

Jaime Allen Monge

First I want to check if there is interaction between the 6LVs--> CAT(EXO) --> Y
If the series of arrows are regression paths, then this is mediation, not moderation/interaction.
I am fairly new to SEM but understand I need to somehow transform the CATS into numbers?

Each exogenous categorical variable can be turned into k - 1 dummy codes, where k = number of categories.  For example, you could turn TIME into 2 dummy codes (PEAK_a and PEAK_m), using "valley" as the reference group.  This is the same method used in multiple regression, so you can find more details online or in an introductory text. 

If you really meant "interaction" (i.e., whether the parameters 6LVs --> Y differ across groups), then you can just use any of the grouping variables to run a multiple-group model, testing interactions by constraining regressions to equality across groups.

I'm not sure I saw a question in there, but your concerns don't seem to have anything to do with lavaan.  Perhaps you should try posting general SEM questions to SEMNET (http://www2.gsu.edu/~mkteer/semnet.html), which is a much larger forum that is also very helpful.

Terry
